title: Shortlist Client Profile — Preview/Tier-Zero Variant (ephemeral, not persisted)
description: Documents the in-memory object POST /api/preview (server.js) builds from a short anonymous form and passes directly to scoreApplication() against every stored JobPosting. Never persisted -- no Prisma model, no database row, exists only for the duration of one request. Written as documentation (and a future test-fixture target once a test suite exists), not as runtime validation on the live request: it's a trusted, server-constructed object, so the risk this guards against is future code drift between server.js and engine/qualification-gate.js, not malformed request input. NOT a $ref subset of client-profile.schema.json -- the required-field sets diverge too much (no name/email/work_authorization/consent, a qualification_bar with only target_seniority, work_history with no entry_id/company/title/bullets) to express as one schema with relaxed 'required'. Instead a sibling schema that reuses shared-defs.schema.json's $defs (skillRef, remotePolicy, money, exclusionCategory, seniorityLevel, dateOrPresent) so the two never drift on primitive vocabulary even though their shapes differ. Every omission/trim documented below was verified against engine/qualification-gate.js's actual field reads (subcon_dataschema consult, q_and_a/.archived) -- each one degrades to a neutral or partial-credit score rather than a hard gate failure or a crash.

basics.description: Trimmed relative to client-profile.basics: no name/email/phone/location/links/work_authorization/notice_period_days (anonymous, pre-signup -- none of those are read by the gate anyway). target_job_titles and target_locations may be empty arrays; unlike client-profile.schema.json this schema does not require minItems:1 on them, since the /api/preview form doesn't enforce either field.

salary_floor.description: Optional -- present only when the visitor enters a salary floor. Absent (not a null/zero placeholder) otherwise, so scoreCompensationFit()'s floorValue==null branch (neutral 6/10) reads as an honest 'unspecified' rather than a real floor of zero.

qualification_bar.description: Optional at the top level -- present only when the visitor picks a target seniority (added commit 06a7bc8; omitted, not set to an 'unspecified'-style value, when they choose 'prefer not to say', so scoreSeniorityFit()'s clientLevel==null neutral fallback stays an honest unknown rather than a mislabeled comparison). Unlike client-profile.qualification_bar, carries only target_seniority -- no must_have_skill_ids/nice_to_have_skill_ids/gate_strictness, none of which the trimmed intake collects and none of which scoreSeniorityFit() reads.

skills.description: Trimmed relative to client-profile.skills: only skill_id + years_experience are collected -- no category/proficiency/last_used/certification_details. Verified safe: clientHasSkill() and scoreRequiredSkillsCoverage() in qualification-gate.js only ever read skill_id and years_experience off a *client's* skill entries; the displayNameFor()/categoryFor() lookups elsewhere in the gate are applied to the *job posting's* required-skill entries for error-message text, never to the client's.

work_history.description: Not real employment records. At most one synthesized entry approximating computeTotalYears()'s expected input from a single 'years of experience' number (empty array if the visitor entered 0). No entry_id/company/title/bullets -- the only reader in qualification-gate.js, computeTotalYears(), uses start_date only.

end_date.description: Always the literal 'present' in the current implementation -- the entry is synthesized as of the request time, not a real end date.

screening_answers.description: Always empty in the current /api/preview implementation -- screening is deferred to a real signup. Kept as its own (empty) array rather than omitted because scoreScreeningCompatibility() in qualification-gate.js reads clientProfile.screening_answers directly; an empty array degrades to partial credit on its own 5%-weighted sub-score, not a hard gate failure. maxItems:0 documents today's reality -- relax this if a future iteration starts collecting a subset of screening answers up front.

exclusions.description: Same field shape as client-profile.exclusions, but every key is always present here (the /api/preview handler always builds the full sub-object) rather than just dealbreakers being required.

excluded_companies.description: Always empty -- not collected in the trimmed intake.

dealbreakers.description: Currently only ever populated with a single weekend_or_oncall_work entry when the visitor checks 'not available for weekends/on-call' -- other exclusion categories aren't collected in the trimmed intake.
